items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...We looked at the lineage: Benny Carter. Looking at of course with Oliver Nelson.

ctx.x: Oliver, the last time I remember working with him was that project with Count Basie. That happened in New York. But everything else that I remember doing with him was in Los Angeles. Then he died suddenly. He would have – I was very privileged to be called by him. A lot of these guys, they were really very busy. I was first call for them at that time, by Quincy and Oliver. Then he passed away. Then it was Quincy and Tom McIntosh. Tom was not so active.

That date with Count Basie was called Afrique. It was recorded in New York in December 1970, Flying Dutchman. I’m going to stay on this subject before I return to the discography. Interviewed Benny Golson for the same program a little while ago. He talked about what it was like being in Los Angeles and writing. We looked at the lineage: Benny Carter. Looking at of course with Oliver Nelson. He talked a lot about Oliver Nelson and how much of a grind it was and how demanding that job was, to work in the industry…
Yes, I was in New York. ’71? Yeah, mostly. I was in New York. I didn’t buy a place here until ’77, ’78, something like that.
